title: The Aurora Roll - the engines play what the clerks found (C2, after the Paul story)
_note: The Reckoning-Works' engines, fed the four wander-finds, play music instead of counting. Each find is a part: Hollis's AURORA is the BELL music-box lead in 'three long folds, then a short one' (h h | h q r); Teague's Snowcune HOP-TRACK is the pluck rhythm (hop hop skiiid hop, rest); Brann's two notes from the rime-lamp's cage are the pad's question-and-answer (A3 -> D4, two bars each); Nib's FROST-FERNS are the pulse12 arpeggio that branches in at bar 9 (bars 9-16: the aurora 'changes its mind'). The engines still tick (soft hat on every beat) - same machines, same care, new meaning. D major, 84 BPM, 16 bars; bar 16 rests on D and the pad's A3 leads back to bar 1. snes era (reverb), 6 voices peak. Also used as the hall's bed once flag:q_works_done is held.
